sources.note: onchain review (no exploit tx in this row; DeFiHackLabs src/test/2022-10/TransitSwap_exp.sol documents the attack. Incident block located by binary-searching eth_getBlockByNumber to measurement.incidentTimestamp -> bsc block 21808649, 2022-10-01T12:00:00Z). The victim 0xed1afc8c4604958c2f38a3408fa63b32e737c428 (unverified, 2820-byte runtime) was created at bsc block 11986161, 2021-10-22T06:52:16Z. It is not a proxy: disassembly shows no DELEGATECALL in the executable region - the single 0xf4 byte a naive opcode scan reports falls inside the trailing CBOR metadata blob - there is no EIP-1967 Upgraded event, and eth_getCode is byte-identical at the creation block and the incident block, so the deployment basis is exact. Its storage slot 0 holds 0xfab745c5ee6c59c09605a40464232930892ba48c (the deploying EOA) unchanged since creation; the remaining slots are an owner/flag pair and a mapping(address => bool) of authorised callers, i.e. configuration, not code. The measurement does not depend on which half of the pair is taken as the victim: the TransitSwap router DeFiHackLabs labels vulnerable, 0x8785bb8deAE13783b24D7aFE250d42eA7D7e9d72, was deployed by the same EOA two minutes later at 2021-10-22T06:54:44Z (block 11986204), giving the same ~344 day age.
exploit tx backfilled and verified onchain (bsc block 21816546, victim in receipt logs), matching the DeFiHackLabs PoC
